iterations.theme: Tijelo kao hram Duha Svetoga: čovjek kao slika Božja, svetost tijela, molitva, čistoća i borba protiv pornografije

sections.subtitle: Čovjek kao vrhunac stvaranja i oholost koja briše sliku Božju
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir Zečević na početku nagovora govori o stvaranju svijeta iz Knjige Postanka
sections.content:
Don Vitomir Zečević nagovor započinje pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija“ i radošću što se okupljeni te večeri nalaze zajedno. Odmah najavljuje temu: **ljudsko tijelo kao hram Duha Svetoga**. Ističe da ono što je Bog darovao pripada Gospodinu, a čovjek se tim darom samo služi.

Polazište traži na prvim stranicama Svetoga pisma, u Knjizi Postanka. Pravi jasnu razliku: **Bog stvara od ničega nešto, a čovjek od nečega stvara nešto.** Bog je stvorio i oblikovao svijet. Sve što stvori je dobro („I vidje Bog da je dobro“), a vrhunac stvaranja je čovjek. Čovjek je slika Božja i potpunost, stvoren s duhom, dušom, tijelom i umom, i tako funkcionira.

Zatim postavlja pitanje koje provlači kroz cijeli nagovor: kada čovjek prestaje biti slika Božja? Odgovor je jednostavan: **kada ne vrši volju Božju.** Kao korijen pada navodi duh oholosti, sažet u latinskom izrazu *non servo*, „ne želim služiti“. Tko odbije služiti Bogu, prestaje biti njegova slika. Don Vitomir to primjenjuje na svakodnevni život: kada su ljudi neposlušni Bogu i žele vršiti svoju volju umjesto njegove, gube tu sličnost.
sections.subtitle_en: Man as the Pinnacle of Creation and the Pride that Erases the Image of God
sections.screenshot_description_en: At the beginning of the talk, Don Vitomir Zečević speaks about the creation of the world from the Book of Genesis
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir Zečević begins the talk with the greeting "Praise be Jesus and Mary" and joy that those gathered are together that evening. He immediately announces the theme: **the human body as a temple of the Holy Spirit**. He points out that what God has given belongs to the Lord, and man merely makes use of that gift.

He seeks his starting point on the first pages of Sacred Scripture, in the Book of Genesis. He makes a clear distinction: **God creates something out of nothing, and man creates something out of something.** God created and shaped the world. Everything He creates is good ("And God saw that it was good"), and the pinnacle of creation is man. Man is the image of God and completeness, created with spirit, soul, body, and mind, and functions as such.

Then he poses a question that he runs through the entire talk: when does man cease to be the image of God? The answer is simple: **when he does not do the will of God.** As the root of the fall, he cites the spirit of pride, summarized in the Latin expression *non servo*, "I will not serve." Whoever refuses to serve God ceases to be His image. Don Vitomir applies this to everyday life: when people are disobedient to God and want to do their own will instead of His, they lose that resemblance.

sections.subtitle: Kada prestaje noć, a počinje dan?
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava prispodobu o učitelju i djeci te izgovara njezinu poantu
sections.content:
Misao o čovjeku kao slici Božjoj don Vitomir ilustrira prispodobom o učitelju koji je djecu pitao kada prestaje noć, a počinje dan.

Prvi se javio dječak i rekao da noć prestaje kada izdaleka vidi drvo, misli da je kruška, a kad priđe, vidi da je šljiva. Učitelj ga je pohvalio, ali odgovor nije prihvatio. Drugi je rekao da je to trenutak kada vidi neku životinju, misli da je magarac, a izbliza vidi da je pas. Učitelj je i taj odgovor ocijenio dobrim, ali netočnim.

Točan je odgovor dao sam učitelj: **„Noć prestaje, a dan počinje kada u svakom čovjeku vidimo sliku Božju.“**

Iz toga don Vitomir izvodi pitanja za osobno preispitivanje: je li svatko od slušatelja danas slika Božja i je li to u vlastitoj obitelji? Naglašava da je ono što Bog stvara i čini uvijek najbolje.
sections.subtitle_en: When Does Night End and Day Begin?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the parable of the teacher and the children and delivers its point
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir illustrates the thought of man as the image of God with a parable about a teacher who asked the children when night ends and day begins.

The first boy spoke up and said that night ends when he sees a tree from afar, thinks it is a pear tree, and when he comes closer, sees that it is a plum tree. The teacher praised him, but did not accept the answer. The second said that it is the moment when he sees an animal, thinks it is a donkey, and from up close sees that it is a dog. The teacher assessed that answer as good as well, but incorrect.

The correct answer was given by the teacher himself: **"Night ends and day begins when we see the image of God in every human being."**

From this, Don Vitomir derives questions for personal examination: is each of the listeners an image of God today, and is he or she that in one's own family? He emphasizes that what God creates and does is always the best.

sections.subtitle: Obitelj koja je zahvaljivala za bolest djeteta
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir pripovijeda kako je paralizirano dijete počelo pomicati prste
sections.content:
Kao primjer kako Bog „pretvara zlo u dobro“, don Vitomir prenosi priču koju mu je ispričao jedan svećenik. Riječ je o obitelji čije je dijete bilo teško bolesno. Roditelji su išli u **Međugorje**, u **Fatimu** i „svugdje“, a onda su došli do jednog svećenika s priznanjem da su sve izmolili i da više ne znaju koju molitvu moliti.

Svećenik im je dao neočekivan savjet: **„Počnite zahvaljivati Bogu za bolest vašeg djeteta.“** Otac je to odbio i ženi rekao da je svećenik lud jer nitko ne zahvaljuje za bolest. Supruga ga je nagovarala da pokušaju i pitala ga je li Isus molio za razbojnike i za one koji su ga tlačili. Kad je potvrdio, predložila je da i oni zahvale Bogu za taj križ.

Kad su počeli tako moliti, dijete koje cijeli život nije moglo dignuti ruku najprije je pomaknulo prste. Roditelji su molili još jače i dijete je ozdravilo i ustalo. Prema don Vitomirovim riječima, bilo je paralizirano dvadeset godina, „od samog svog začeća“. Oboje roditelja zaplakalo je: „Kako je Bog velik! Kako Bog pretvara zlo u dobro!“

Don Vitomir zaključuje da Bog na isti način želi **od grešnika napraviti sveca**.
sections.subtitle_en: A Family that Gave Thanks for the Illness of a Child
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir recounts how a paralyzed child began to move fingers
sections.content_en:
As an example of how God "turns evil into good," Don Vitomir conveys a story told to him by a priest. It is about a family whose child was gravely ill. The parents went to **Međugorje**, to **Fatima**, and "everywhere," and then they came to a priest with the admission that they had prayed everything and no longer knew what prayer to pray.

The priest gave them unexpected advice: **"Begin giving thanks to God for the illness of your child."** The father refused this and told his wife that the priest was crazy because nobody gives thanks for an illness. The wife urged him to try and asked him whether Jesus prayed for the robbers and for those who oppressed Him. When he affirmed it, she suggested that they too give thanks to God for that cross.

When they began praying like that, the child, who could not raise a hand for its entire life, first moved its fingers. The parents prayed even harder and the child was healed and stood up. According to Don Vitomir's words, the child had been paralyzed for twenty years, "from its very conception." Both parents wept: "How great God is! How God turns evil into good!"

Don Vitomir concludes that in the same way God wants **to make a saint out of a sinner**.

sections.subtitle: Pretvorba kao Kalvarija i euharistijska čuda od Ludbrega do Coimbre
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o euharistijskom čudu u portugalskoj Coimbri
sections.content:
Pretvorbu na svetoj misi don Vitomir naziva **najsvetijim činom**. Kad svećenik ispruži ruku nad običnim kruhom i vinom, oni samo po molitvi da siđe Duh Sveti postaju tijelo i krv Kristova. U istom trenutku, objašnjava, svećenik moli i za vjernike: da grešnici, među koje ubraja i sebe, postanu sveci, a bolesnici zdravi. Zato poziva: „Tko god može, neka klekne.“ U tom trenutku je Kalvarija i Isus daje sebe.

Podsjeća da je kroz povijest „jako puno“ svećenika posumnjalo da je u kaležu doista krv Kristova, pa su u vinu ugledali krv. Spominje euharistijsko čudo u **Ludbregu** i čuda u **Lancianu**.

Posebno opširno prepričava događaj iz portugalskog mjesta **Coimbra**, za koji je čuo na hodočašću:

- Muž je živio razvratnim životom, a žena je umjesto svećeniku otišla gatari.
- Gatara je tražila da joj donese posvećenu hostiju.
- Žena je nakon pričesti izvadila hostiju iz usta i stavila je u kecelju, a tada je počela teći krv, sve od crkve do kuće.
- Hostiju je sakrila u sanduk. Navečer je muž vidio da sanduk sjaji, a ona je priznala što je učinila.
- Hostija je odnesena svećeniku, a prema don Vitomirovim riječima pretvorila se u tijelo Isusovo, „srce koje otkucava“.

To uspoređuje s Lancianom, gdje se, kako kaže, čuva srčani mišić koji kuca kao srce.
sections.subtitle_en: The Consecration as Calvary and Eucharistic Miracles from Ludbreg to Coimbra
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the Eucharistic miracle in Portuguese Coimbra
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir calls the consecration at Holy Mass **the holiest act**. When the priest extends his hand over the ordinary bread and wine, solely through the prayer that the Holy Spirit descend, they become the body and blood of Christ. At the same moment, he explains, the priest also prays for the faithful: that sinners, among whom he includes himself, become saints, and the sick become healthy. That is why he calls out: "Whoever can, let him kneel." At that moment it is Calvary and Jesus gives Himself.

He recalls that throughout history "very many" priests doubted that the blood of Christ was truly in the chalice, and so they saw blood in the wine. He mentions the Eucharistic miracle in **Ludbreg** and the miracles in **Lanciano**.

He recounts particularly extensively an event from the Portuguese town of **Coimbra**, about which he heard on a pilgrimage:

- The husband lived a debauched life, and the wife went to a fortune teller instead of a priest.
- The fortune teller demanded that she bring her a consecrated Host.
- After Communion, the woman took the Host out of her mouth and put it in her apron, and then blood began to flow, all the way from the church to the house.
- She hid the Host in a chest. In the evening, the husband saw the chest shining, and she confessed what she had done.
- The Host was taken to a priest, and according to Don Vitomir's words it turned into the body of Jesus, "a beating heart."

He compares this with Lanciano, where, as he says, a heart muscle is preserved that beats like a heart.

sections.subtitle: Posvećenje i odvažnost po primjeru svetog Nikole Tavelića
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir govori o svetom Nikoli Taveliću i pozivu na hrabro svjedočenje
sections.content:
Za današnjeg vjernika don Vitomir kao ključnu riječ ističe **posvećenje**: posvetiti se svojoj obitelji i moliti krunicu za domovinu i obitelj. Mišljenje drugih proglašava nebitnim. Bitno je što će reći Bog, koji bi mogao prigovoriti: „Mogao si, a nisi učinio. Trebao si izaći, a nisi učinio.“

Kao uzor navodi **svetog Nikolu Tavelića**, koji je izašao pred muslimanskog vođu i naviještao živoga Isusa Krista. „Nije morao, ali htio je“, kaže don Vitomir, a Isus ga je pozvao da svjedoči svojom krvlju.

Okupljenima poručuje da **Bog traži odvažne i hrabre**. Podsjeća da Isus nije odjednom pozvao stotinu ljudi, nego učenike dvojicu po dvojicu. Zaključuje: „Nije važna količina i koliko nas je, nego kakvi smo ljudi i kakvi smo vjernici.“
sections.subtitle_en: Dedication and Boldness Following the Example of Saint Nikola Tavelić
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir speaks about Saint Nikola Tavelić and the call to courageous witness
sections.content_en:
For the believer of today, Don Vitomir emphasizes **dedication** as the key word: to dedicate oneself to one's family and pray the Rosary for the homeland and family. He declares the opinion of others to be irrelevant. What matters is what God will say, who could reproach: "You could have, but you did not do it. You should have gone out, but you did not do it."

As a role model, he cites **Saint Nikola Tavelić**, who went out before the Muslim leader and proclaimed the living Jesus Christ. "He did not have to, but he wanted to," says Don Vitomir, and Jesus called him to witness with his blood.

He tells those gathered that **God seeks the bold and the courageous**. He recalls that Jesus did not call a hundred people at once, but disciples two by two. He concludes: "What matters is not the quantity and how many of us there are, but what kind of people we are and what kind of believers we are."

sections.subtitle: Od starozavjetnog šatora do hrama u čovjeku
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira poslanicu svetog Pavla Korinćanima o tijelu kao hramu Duha Svetoga
sections.content:
U središte nagovora don Vitomir stavlja riječi **svetog Pavla**: „Ili zar ne znate? Tijelo vaše hram je Duha Svetoga koji je u vama, koga imate od Boga.“ Iz toga slijedi da vjernik treba **proslaviti Boga svojim tijelom**.

Objašnjava i kontekst. U zajednici u Korintu bilo je mnogo razvrata i grešnosti, pa ih je Pavao pozivao da ukrote svoje udove i tijelo i stave ga u službu Boga. Božji darovi trebaju služiti Bogu, životu, obitelji i novom životu.

Pojam hrama tumači starozavjetnom slikom. Židovi su najprije imali **šator**, a zatim hram u kojem se čuvalo Deset Božjih zapovijedi, kao znak da je Gospodin s njima. Spominje i Mojsija: dok je podizao ruke, narod je pobjeđivao, a kad bi ih spustio od umora, gubio je. Za don Vitomira to je znak Božje prisutnosti. **Hram je mjesto gdje je Bog prisutan.** Za vjernike je to crkva, ali i vlastito tijelo, jer je Bog čovjeku pri stvaranju udahnuo svoj dah.

Zatim nabraja kada Bog **nije** u čovjeku:

- kada je čovjek u teškom, smrtnom grijehu,
- kada ne oprašta,
- kada mu Bog nije na prvom mjestu,
- kada ode vračaru ili hodži.

Tada se, upozorava, život „ide skroz ulijevo“. Pavlovu poruku sažima ovako: tijelo je stvorio Bog, ono je slika Božja i u njemu Bog prebiva, zato od njega ne treba „činiti nakazu“.
sections.subtitle_en: From the Old Testament Tent to the Temple in Man
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes Saint Paul's epistle to the Corinthians about the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
At the center of the talk, Don Vitomir places the words of **Saint Paul**: "Or do you not know? Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God." From this it follows that the believer should **glorify God with his body**.

He also explains the context. In the community in Corinth there was much debauchery and sinfulness, so Paul urged them to tame their members and body and place it in the service of God. God's gifts should serve God, life, family, and new life.

He interprets the concept of the temple through an Old Testament image. The Jews first had a **tent**, and then a temple in which the Ten Commandments were kept, as a sign that the Lord was with them. He also mentions Moses: while he held up his hands, the people prevailed, and when he lowered them from exhaustion, they lost. For Don Vitomir, this is a sign of God's presence. **The temple is the place where God is present.** For believers, it is the church, but also their own body, because at creation God breathed His breath into man.

Then he enumerates when God is **not** in man:

- when man is in grave, mortal sin,
- when he does not forgive,
- when God is not in first place for him,
- when he goes to a sorcerer or a hodja.

Then, he warns, life "goes completely to the left." He summarizes Paul's message like this: the body was created by God, it is the image of God and God dwells in it, therefore one should not "make a monstrosity" out of it.

sections.subtitle: Riječ je tijelom postala: utjelovljenje, Trojstvo i opasnost samoće
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir prepričava riječi starijih ljudi iz staračkog doma o samoći
sections.content:
Najdublji razlog kršćanskog poštovanja tijela don Vitomir vidi u **Isusu Kristu** i otajstvu utjelovljenja koje naviješta Evanđelje po Ivanu: Božja Riječ postala je tijelom i nastanila se među nama.

To začinjava anegdotom o jednom sinjskom fratru koji je bio u **Nazaretu** (i sam don Vitomir ondje je bio na hodočašću). Majka ga je nazvala iz Sinja i pitala gdje je, a on je odgovorio da je upravo u spilji gdje je anđeo pozdravio Mariju, baš u trenutku kad će ona izmoliti Zdravo Marijo.

Govoreći o **Presvetom Trojstvu**, priznaje granice ljudskog razuma: čovjek ima „plafon, strop“, a dalje ide vjera. Ipak nudi pojednostavljenu sliku: **Bog Otac zamišlja, Bog Sin govori, a Bog Duh Sveti izvršava.** Bog je jedan, ali trojstven. Ni on ne želi biti sam, pa ne želi ni da ljudi budu sami.

To povezuje s iskustvom iz posjeta staračkom domu, gdje mu stariji ljudi govore: „Velečasni, najteže mi je biti sam.“ Don Vitomir upozorava da **samoća najviše ubija čovjeka**. U njoj dolaze suicidalne misli, navaljuje grijeh, rađaju se fantazije i prepuštanje sebi, pa čovjek gubi kontrolu nad sobom.

Podsjeća i da je Isus u potpunosti prihvatio ljudsku tjelesnost. Rodio se kao dijete kojemu je trebala majčina briga, rastao je, učio, radio i hodao putevima. Osjećao je glad i žeđ, umarao se i plakao, a u Getsemanskom vrtu proživio je tjeskobu kao čovjek. Tijelo mu je bilo izranjeno i probodeno, a ipak je do kraja izvršio volju Očevu. Taj se Krist i danas daruje pod prilikama kruha i vina.
sections.subtitle_en: The Word Became Flesh: The Incarnation, the Trinity, and the Danger of Solitude
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir recounts the words of elderly people from a nursing home about solitude
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir sees the deepest reason for Christian respect for the body in **Jesus Christ** and the mystery of the Incarnation proclaimed by the Gospel of John: the Word of God became flesh and dwelt among us.

He spices this with an anecdote about a friar from Sinj who was in **Nazareth** (Don Vitomir himself was there on a pilgrimage). His mother called him from Sinj and asked where he was, and he answered that he was right in the cave where the angel greeted Mary, at the very moment when she was about to pray the Hail Mary.

Speaking of the **Holy Trinity**, he acknowledges the limits of human reason: man has a "ceiling, roof," and beyond that goes faith. Still, he offers a simplified image: **God the Father envisions, God the Son speaks, and God the Holy Spirit accomplishes.** God is one, but triune. He does not want to be alone either, so He does not want people to be alone either.

He connects this with the experience from visits to a nursing home, where elderly people tell him: "Reverend, the hardest thing for me is being alone." Don Vitomir warns that **solitude kills man the most**. In it come suicidal thoughts, sin rushes in, fantasies and self-indulgence are born, and so man loses control over himself.

He also recalls that Jesus completely accepted human bodily reality. He was born as a child who needed a mother's care, He grew, learned, worked, and walked the roads. He felt hunger and thirst, grew tired and wept, and in the Garden of Gethsemane He experienced agony as a man. His body was wounded and pierced, and yet He accomplished the Father's will to the end. That same Christ gives Himself today under the appearances of bread and wine.

sections.subtitle: Tijelo osjeti ispovijed: veza duhovnog i tjelesnog zdravlja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o analizi zdravstvenih pokazatelja sudionika duhovne obnove
sections.content:
Iz utjelovljenja don Vitomir izvodi zaključak da je **tijelo svetost** i da se za njega treba brinuti, pa i duhovno. Kad je čovjek loše volje, u srdžbi, psovci ili mržnji, to osjeti i njegovo tijelo.

Navodi primjer svećenika koji je mjerio tlak, rad srca i šećer kod sudionika duhovne obnove prije i nakon nje. Prema don Vitomirovim riječima, razlika je bila „drastična“. Tijelo osjeti ispovijed, molitvu, klanjanje i krunicu Božjeg milosrđa: postaje mirno i staloženo. Napetost i srdžba pak u tijelu ostavljaju trag.

Prenosi i tvrdnju da, „kako ljudi većinom kažu“, **70 posto tjelesnih bolesti dolazi od bolesti duha i duše**. Uzroke vidi u tome što su ljudi nesretni, ne ispovijedaju se temeljito, ne predaju se Gospodinu i ne mole. Takvog čovjeka, kaže, svjetovno „uhvati, obori, vodi i zavodi“, pa se udaljava od Boga.
sections.subtitle_en: The Body Senses Confession: The Connection Between Spiritual and Physical Health
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the analysis of health indicators of spiritual retreat participants
sections.content_en:
From the Incarnation, Don Vitomir derives the conclusion that **the body is sacredness** and that one should care for it, including spiritually. When a person is in a bad mood, in anger, swearing, or hatred, his body senses that as well.

He cites the example of a priest who measured blood pressure, heart rate, and blood sugar in participants of a spiritual retreat before and after it. According to Don Vitomir's words, the difference was "drastic." The body senses confession, prayer, Eucharistic adoration, and the Chaplet of Divine Mercy: it becomes calm and composed. Tension and anger, on the other hand, leave a mark in the body.

He also conveys the assertion that, "as people mostly say," **70 percent of physical illnesses come from illnesses of the spirit and soul**. He sees the causes in the fact that people are unhappy, do not confess thoroughly, do not surrender themselves to the Lord, and do not pray. Such a person, he says, is "caught, struck down, led, and seduced" by the worldly, and so moves away from God.

sections.subtitle: „Nemam vremena za sebe“ i „Ja sam gospodar svoga tijela“
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir odbacuje tvrdnju da je čovjek gospodar svoga tijela
sections.content:
Don Vitomir osvrće se na rečenicu koju često čuje: **„Nemam vremena za sebe.“** Ljudi imaju vremena za sve drugo, ali ne za svoju nutrinu, molitvu i djecu, pa im se čini kao da im stalno nešto nedostaje. Iza toga vidi napast zloga, koji čovjeku stavlja u glavu da je nešto drugo važnije i preče.

Odlučno odbacuje i stav **„Ja sam gospodar svoga tijela“**. Gospodar je Bog, koji je čovjeku dao tijelo i oblikovao ga na svoju sliku. Svaki je čovjek jedinstvena slika Božja: „**Nema kopije. Mi smo svi originalna slika.**“ Zato nitko nema pravo uništavati svoje tijelo.

Potrebno je, ističe, najprije imati vremena za sebe i ljubiti sebe, a onda ljubiti druge. To znači posvetiti se sebi, obitelji i vlastitoj izgradnji te ispitati savjest.

Opisuje i tipična jutra: prva misao su brige o poslu, o liječničkoj dijagnozi i o onome što čeka tijekom dana. Razlog vidi u tome što ljudi ne mole dobro i ne predaju brige Gospodinu, nego misle da sve mogu sami. „Ne možeš. Tijelo to trpi“, upozorava. Takav je čovjek „van sebe“, ili, kako kažu Bosanci, „nije u vinklu“.
sections.subtitle_en: "I Have No Time for Myself" and "I Am the Master of My Body"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir rejects the assertion that man is the master of his body
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir reflects on a sentence he often hears: **"I have no time for myself."** People have time for everything else, but not for their interior life, prayer, and children, so it seems to them as if they are constantly lacking something. Behind this he sees the temptation of the evil one, who puts it into man's head that something else is more important and more urgent.

He also resolutely rejects the attitude **"I am the master of my body"**. The master is God, who gave man a body and shaped him in His image. Every human being is a unique image of God: "**There is no copy. We are all an original image.**" Therefore, no one has the right to destroy his own body.

It is necessary, he emphasizes, first to have time for oneself and to love oneself, and then to love others. That means dedicating oneself to oneself, family, and one's own edification, and examining one's conscience.

He also describes typical mornings: the first thought is worries about work, about a doctor's diagnosis, and about what awaits during the day. He sees the reason in the fact that people do not pray well and do not surrender their worries to the Lord, but think that they can do everything on their own. "You cannot. The body suffers that," he warns. Such a person is "beside himself," or, as Bosnians say, "not in plumb."

sections.subtitle: Inventura srca: ispit savjesti i kratke molitve za večer i jutro
sections.screenshot_description: Gost izgovara primjer kratke večernje molitve
sections.content:
Don Vitomir preporučuje da svatko navečer prije spavanja napravi **„inventuru svoga srca“**. Predlaže konkretna pitanja:

- Jesam li se sjetio Boga? Jesam li izmolio Anđeo Gospodnji i jutarnju molitvu?
- Jesam li se zahvalio Bogu?
- Kakav je moj odnos prema supruzi i kolegama na poslu? Jesam li bio ljut, grub, srdit, jesam li odgovarao ili mrzio?
- Jesam li mogao danas ići na svetu misu? Jesam li se mogao ispovjediti?

Nakon toga slijedi kajanje i molitva „Ispovijedam se Bogu svemogućem“.

Nudi i primjer kratke **večernje molitve**: „Gospodine, hvala ti za ovaj dan što si bio sa mnom. Blagoslovi ovu noć da mogu mirno spavati, bez uznemiravanja zla. I daj da se ujutro mogu probuditi s tobom. Amen.“

Za **jutro** predlaže pozdrav Isusu: „Dobro jutro, Isuse. Dobro došao u moju sobu. Dobro došao u ovaj dan. Hvala ti za jučerašnji dan i ovu noć što si bio sa mnom. Koliko se nije ljudi diglo, ja sam se digao. Hvala ti.“ Uz to se može izmoliti i Anđeo Gospodnji. Obećava da će se plodovi vidjeti, jer je to osobna molitva u kojoj čovjek sam moli i zahvaljuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Inventory of the Heart: Examination of Conscience and Short Prayers for Evening and Morning
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks an example of a short evening prayer
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir recommends that everyone make an **"inventory of one's heart"** in the evening before sleep. He suggests concrete questions:

- Did I remember God? Did I pray the Angelus and the morning prayer?
- Did I give thanks to God?
- What is my relationship toward my wife and colleagues at work? Was I angry, harsh, wrathful, did I talk back or hate?
- Could I have gone to Holy Mass today? Could I have gone to confession?

After that follow contrition and the prayer "I confess to almighty God."

He also offers an example of a short **evening prayer**: "Lord, thank you for this day, that You were with me. Bless this night so that I can sleep peacefully, without the disturbance of evil. And grant that in the morning I may wake up with You. Amen."

For the **morning** he suggests a greeting to Jesus: "Good morning, Jesus. Welcome to my room. Welcome to this day. Thank you for yesterday and this night, that You were with me. So many people did not get up, but I got up. Thank you." Along with that, the Angelus can also be prayed. He promises that the fruits will be seen, because it is a personal prayer in which man prays and gives thanks himself.

sections.subtitle: Molitva koja mijenja: ne uspoređuj se i ustraj
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir pripovijeda o hodži koji se obratio čitajući Kur'an
sections.content:
Don Vitomir naglašava da **molitva mora preoblikovati i mijenjati čovjeka**. Razlikuje one koji mole, ali „brbljaju“, od onih koji znaju moliti u Duhu Svetom i traže od Gospodina pomoć da dobro žive i razumiju.

Upozorava na sklonost **uspoređivanju s drugima**: netko ima bolje tijelo, bolji je ili zdraviji. „Ti nisi kopija. Ti si original. Bog je tebe tako stvorio“, poručuje. Navodi primjer žena koje kažu da su drugi napravili kuću ili digli kredit, pa mogu i oni. Savjetuje narodnom mudrošću: **„Pokrij se dekom koliko je široka.“**

Isus se, podsjeća, ni s kim nije uspoređivao. Pitao je učenike što ljudi govore tko je on, a zatim što oni misle. Nakon tišine samo je Petar ispovjedio da je on Pomazanik, Sin Božji. Isus mu je odgovorio da to nije rekao sam od sebe, nego mu je to dao Duh Božji.

Kao primjer obraćenja prepričava priču o hodži koji je postao katolik čitajući **Kur'an**. Ondje je pročitao da je Isus kao dijete oživljavao glinene golubove. Zaključio je da to može samo Bog, dakle da je Isus Bog, i promijenio je život.

Iz toga izvodi poruku o **ustrajnoj molitvi**: ne mijenja čovjek svoju ženu, djecu ili bližnje, nego Bog, na molitvu koja traje mjesecima i godinama. S humorom navodi primjer susjeda koji svaki dan u tri sata ujutro svira gitaru. Umjesto ljutnje preporučuje molitvu: „Gospodine, promijeni ga na bolje.“
sections.subtitle_en: Prayer that Changes: Do Not Compare Yourself and Persevere
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir recounts a story about a hodja who converted reading the Quran
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir emphasizes that **prayer must transform and change man**. He distinguishes between those who pray, but "babble," and those who know how to pray in the Holy Spirit and ask the Lord for help to live well and understand.

He warns against the tendency to **compare oneself with others**: someone has a better body, is better, or healthier. "You are not a copy. You are an original. God created you like that," he conveys. He cites the example of women who say that others built a house or took out a loan, so they can too. He advises with folk wisdom: **"Cover yourself with the blanket as far as it reaches."**

Jesus, he recalls, did not compare Himself with anyone. He asked the disciples what people say who He is, and then what they think. After the silence, only Peter confessed that He is the Anointed One, the Son of God. Jesus answered him that he did not say this on his own, but the Spirit of God gave it to him.

As an example of conversion, he recounts the story of a hodja who became Catholic reading the **Quran**. There he read that Jesus as a child brought clay pigeons to life. He concluded that only God can do that, therefore that Jesus is God, and he changed his life.

From this he derives a message about **persevering prayer**: man does not change his wife, children, or neighbors, but God does, in response to prayer that lasts for months and years. With humor he cites the example of a neighbor who plays the guitar every day at three in the morning. Instead of anger, he recommends prayer: "Lord, change him for the better."

sections.subtitle: Estetska kirurgija, tetovaže i piercinzi: preoblikovanje Božjeg hrama
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na pitanje vjernika o tetovaži s likom Isusa ili krunicom
sections.content:
Drugi dio nagovora don Vitomir posvećuje nezadovoljstvu vlastitim izgledom. Ljudi, kaže, mijenjaju uši i nosove i odlaze na **estetsku kirurgiju** jer žele biti netko drugi. Time, prema njegovim riječima, ne žele biti djeca Božja. Poziva na prihvaćanje: Bog je nekome dao takvu frizuru, nekome da nema kose, i to treba prihvatiti kao vlastiti križ. Treba prihvatiti i bolest, različitost i patnju, uz svijest da Duh Sveti vodi čovjeka. Ako ga čovjek makne i dođe zli duh, on razara najprije njega, a zatim njegovu obitelj i djecu.

Posebno se osvrće na **tetovaže**. Na pitanja vjernika koji su istetovirali lik Isusa ili krunicu odgovara: „Ništa ne stavljaj. To nije kršćanski oblik.“ Smatra da se time tijelo unakazuje i da se ne znaju posljedice, primjerice za krv. Ne podržava ni slike i natpise na koži jer je čovjek hram Duha Svetoga i ne treba ga preoblikovati. Dodaje da i to treba ispovijedati.

Isto vrijedi za **piercinge**. Iza svega vidi želju za oponašanjem, poistovjećivanjem s nogometašima ili drugim uzorima, i podložnost trendu, uključujući i modu puštanja brade. Poruku sažima ovako: **„Bog želi tvoje lice vidjeti. Sliku tvoju.“**
sections.subtitle_en: Cosmetic Surgery, Tattoos, and Piercings: Reshaping God's Temple
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers a believer's question about a tattoo with the image of Jesus or a Rosary
sections.content_en:
The second part of the talk Don Vitomir devotes to dissatisfaction with one's own appearance. People, he says, change their ears and noses and go for **cosmetic surgery** because they want to be someone else. Thereby, according to his words, they do not want to be children of God. He calls for acceptance: God gave someone such a hairstyle, someone to have no hair, and that should be accepted as one's own cross. One should also accept illness, diversity, and suffering, with the awareness that the Holy Spirit leads man. If man removes Him and an evil spirit comes, it destroys him first, and then his family and children.

He reflects specifically on **tattoos**. To questions from believers who had tattooed the image of Jesus or a Rosary, he replies: "Do not put anything on. That is not a Christian form." He considers that the body is thereby disfigured and that the consequences are not known, for example for the blood. Nor does he support images and inscriptions on the skin because man is a temple of the Holy Spirit and should not be reshaped. He adds that this too should be confessed.

The same applies to **piercings**. Behind everything he sees a desire for imitation, identification with soccer players or other role models, and subjection to trends, including the fashion of growing a beard. He summarizes the message like this: **"God wants to see your face. Your image."**

sections.subtitle: Pornografija kao teret današnjih muškaraca
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir govori o pornografiji i očima kao vratima grijeha
sections.content:
Don Vitomir poziva na brigu o **spolnosti**, koju je Bog dao čovjeku. Kao veliko opterećenje s kojim se danas suočavaju muškarci navodi **pornografiju**, mjesto gdje ljudi „umaraju“ i „ranjavaju“ svoje oči.

Objašnjava kako grijeh nastaje: **oči su vrata** kroz koja ulazi slika. Slika ulazi u misli, spušta se u srce i završava u činu, u samozadovoljavanju, jer takva slika unosi nemir.

Prenosi i podatke iz jednog američkog istraživanja o ljudima koji se bave snimanjem pornografije: prema njegovim riječima, u godinu dana njih „50, 60“ počinilo je samoubojstvo, završilo u drogi ili psihički stradalo. Zaključuje da pornografija **razara mozak, srce i zdrav odnos prema spolnosti**.

Prenosi i riječi jednog svećenika karizmatika da je nakon odricanja od pornografije potrebno **pet godina** da čovjek obnovi stanice, misli, život i zdrav odnos prema ženi i vlastitom spolu.
sections.subtitle_en: Pornography as a Burden of Today's Men
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir speaks about pornography and the eyes as the doorway to sin
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir calls for care regarding **sexuality**, which God gave to man. As a great burden that men face today, he cites **pornography**, a place where people "tire" and "wound" their eyes.

He explains how sin originates: **the eyes are the door** through which the image enters. The image enters the thoughts, descends into the heart, and ends in the act, in masturbation, because such an image introduces unrest.

He also conveys data from an American study about people involved in filming pornography: according to his words, in one year "50, 60" of them committed suicide, ended up in drugs, or suffered psychological damage. He concludes that pornography **destroys the brain, the heart, and a healthy attitude toward sexuality**.

He also conveys the words of a charismatic priest that after renouncing pornography it takes **five years** for a person to restore cells, thoughts, life, and a healthy relationship toward women and one's own sex.

sections.subtitle: Spolnost kao čežnja za nježnošću koju daje Bog
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o spolnosti kao želji za blizinom i o nježnosti Božjoj
sections.content:
Don Vitomir spolnost definira kao **želju za blizinom i nježnošću**. Tu čežnju, kaže, u punini može ispuniti Bog. Poziva vjernike da osjete nježnost kojom ih vole Gospa i Isus, posebno u ispovjedaonici, gdje dobivaju oproštenje i odlaze u miru. Takvu nježnost može dati samo Bog Otac, koji čovjeka nježno voli.

Kao svjedoka navodi **svetog Augustina**, kojemu je, kako kaže, trebalo trideset godina da se obrati. On je u *Ispovijestima* pisao o nježnosti Božjoj, a don Vitomir prenosi njegovu misao: „U tebi sam pronašao mir. U tebi sam pronašao nježnost. O, Gospodine, moje se srce smirilo u tebi.“ Srce je prije toga lutalo posvuda, kao što i svaki čovjek luta i traži.
sections.subtitle_en: Sexuality as a Longing for Tenderness Given by God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about sexuality as a desire for closeness and about the tenderness of God
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir defines sexuality as a **desire for closeness and tenderness**. That longing, he says, can be fulfilled in fullness by God. He invites believers to feel the tenderness with which Our Lady and Jesus love them, especially in the confessional, where they receive forgiveness and leave in peace. Such tenderness can only be given by God the Father, who tenderly loves man.

As a witness, he cites **Saint Augustine**, who, as he says, took thirty years to convert. In the *Confessions*, he wrote about the tenderness of God, and Don Vitomir conveys his thought: "In You I found peace. In You I found tenderness. Oh, Lord, my heart has rested in You." Before that, the heart wandered everywhere, just as every human being wanders and searches.

sections.subtitle: „Isus je najbolji oftalmolog“: bolest i duh straha
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir pripovijeda o svećeniku kojemu je dijagnosticiran karcinom oka
sections.content:
Bolest, napominje don Vitomir, mijenja i oblik tijela. Čovjek ode liječniku zdrav, vrati se bolestan, a s dijagnozom prvo dođe **duh straha** i pitanje: „Kako ću ja to?“

Kao primjer navodi svećenika **Marka**, kojemu je nedavno dijagnosticiran karcinom oka. Odmah se pomislilo na najgore, a don Vitomir mu je savjetovao: „Idi prvo Isusu predaj. Isus je najbolji oftalmolog. On ti najbolje zna.“

Marko je operiran nekoliko dana ranije „gore na Rebru“ i rekao je da će mu, čini se, spasiti oko. Don Vitomir mu je odgovorio da ga neće spasiti liječnik, nego Isus, koji djeluje preko **doktora Vukojevića**. S osmijehom prenosi Markove riječi da je trebao šutjeti tri dana, ali nije mogao jer je bio „manji od makovog zrna“. Don Vitomir mu je rekao da su molili za njega. Dodaje da je Marko te večeri trebao ispovijedati okupljene, ali sada moli za njih.

Odatle izvodi praktičan savjet: **svaku lošu vijest najprije predati Isusu.** Misao ili sumnja ulazi u mozak, iz mozga u srce, a iz srca u život. Kad netko dojavi tračeve ili laži, ne treba im vjerovati, nego reći: „Isuse, ja to predajem, a ti njega promijeni.“ Inače u srce ulaze mržnja, srdžba i psovka. Zaključuje: ne dopustiti da se misao, osobito negativna, pretvori u djelo.
sections.subtitle_en: "Jesus Is the Best Ophthalmologist": Illness and the Spirit of Fear
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir recounts a story about a priest diagnosed with eye cancer
sections.content_en:
Illness, Don Vitomir notes, also changes the shape of the body. A person goes to the doctor healthy, returns sick, and with the diagnosis first comes the **spirit of fear** and the question: "How will I handle that?"

As an example, he cites the priest **Marko**, who was recently diagnosed with eye cancer. Immediately the worst was thought, and Don Vitomir advised him: "Go first and surrender it to Jesus. Jesus is the best ophthalmologist. He knows you best."

Marko was operated on a few days earlier "up at Rebro" and said that, it seems, they will save his eye. Don Vitomir answered him that not the doctor, but Jesus, who acts through **Dr. Vukojević**, will save it. With a smile, he conveys Marko's words that he was supposed to keep silent for three days, but could not because he was "smaller than a poppy seed." Don Vitomir told him that they prayed for him. He adds that Marko was supposed to hear confessions of those gathered that evening, but now he is praying for them.

From that he derives practical advice: **first surrender every piece of bad news to Jesus.** A thought or doubt enters the brain, from the brain into the heart, and from the heart into life. When someone reports gossip or lies, one should not believe them, but say: "Jesus, I surrender this, and You change him." Otherwise, hatred, anger, and swearing enter the heart. He concludes: do not allow a thought, especially a negative one, to turn into an action.

sections.subtitle: Ruke, jezik i pogled u službi Boga: važnije je što kaže Bog nego ulica
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi misao svetog Augustina o susretu s Gospodinom
sections.content:
Tijelo treba preoblikovati tako da u njemu bude Bog, odnosno da bude „stavljeno u opticaj za Gospodina“. Don Vitomir ističe da je izbor uvijek na čovjeku: **ruke** mogu činiti dobro ili zlo, a **jezik** može dati blagoslov ili prokletstvo, hvaliti ili psovati Boga, vrijeđati ili ohrabriti. Kao primjer navodi pohvalu okupljenima: „Gledaj kako su ovi muški hrabri, jaki, snažni.“

Poziva da se ne ravna prema onome što kaže „ulica“ i mediji, nego prema onome što će Bog reći kad čovjek dođe pred njega. Prenosi odgovor **svetog Augustina** na pitanje što bi mu bilo najteže: doći pred Gospodina i da Gospodin prođe pokraj njega, a da ga ne vidi i ne primijeti.

„Bog me vidi. Ja Bogu služim“, naglašava don Vitomir, čak i ako ljudi i mediji pljuju, a supruga prigovara: „Šta ideš tamo, čovječe Božji, sjedni ovdje, moli ovdje.“ Podsjeća da je i Isus mogao odbiti križ, ali je u Getsemaniju molio da bude volja Očeva.
sections.subtitle_en: Hands, Tongue, and Gaze in the Service of God: What God Says Matters More than the Street
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys Saint Augustine's thought about the encounter with the Lord
sections.content_en:
The body should be reshaped so that God is in it, that is, that it is "placed into circulation for the Lord." Don Vitomir emphasizes that the choice is always up to man: **hands** can do good or evil, and the **tongue** can give a blessing or a curse, praise or blaspheme God, insult or encourage. As an example, he mentions praise to those gathered: "Look at how brave, strong, powerful these men are."

He urges not to be guided by what "the street" and the media say, but by what God will say when man comes before Him. He conveys the response of **Saint Augustine** to the question of what would be hardest for him: to come before the Lord and have the Lord pass by him without seeing or noticing him.

"God sees me. I serve God," Don Vitomir emphasizes, even if people and the media spit, and the wife complains: "Why are you going there, man of God, sit here, pray here." He recalls that Jesus too could have refused the cross, but in Gethsemane He prayed that the Father's will be done.

sections.subtitle: Zrinski, Merc, Tavelić i Stepinac: hrabrost čiste savjesti
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir nabraja hrabre ljude vjere iz hrvatske povijesti
sections.content:
Don Vitomir okupljenima poručuje da je Božja volja da dođu i pokažu svijetu, Hrvatskoj i svojim gradovima da postoje hrabri ljudi vjere. Povezuje to s onima koji su bili hrabri u obrani domovine i nabraja uzore:

- **Zrinski**
- **Ivan Merc**
- **Nikola Tavelić**
- **Alojzije Stepinac**

Osobito ističe Stepinca, koji je mogao popustiti, ali nije. Don Vitomir mu pripisuje stav: „Vi me možete osuditi, ali moja savjest je mirna i čista.“

To prenosi na slušatelje: važno je ići s dobrom namjerom, imati čistu savjest i biti **sakramentalno povezan**. Upozorava da će brige i poteškoće rasti što više budu molili i okupljali se. Ipak ih hrabri: „Puno toga lomite. Vi spašavate mnoge duše u molitvi.“ Poziva ih da mole za svoje drage, pokojne, bolesne i za sve ljude.
sections.subtitle_en: Zrinski, Merz, Tavelić, and Stepinac: The Courage of a Clear Conscience
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir enumerates courageous people of faith from Croatian history
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir tells those gathered that it is God's will for them to come and show the world, Croatia, and their cities that courageous people of faith exist. He connects this with those who were courageous in defending the homeland and enumerates role models:

- **Zrinski**
- **Ivan Merz**
- **Nikola Tavelić**
- **Alojzije Stepinac**

He particularly emphasizes Stepinac, who could have yielded, but did not. Don Vitomir attributes to him the attitude: "You can condemn me, but my conscience is peaceful and clear."

He transfers this to the listeners: it is important to go with good intentions, to have a clear conscience, and to be **sacramentally connected**. He warns that worries and difficulties will grow the more they pray and gather. Still, he encourages them: "You are breaking a lot of things. You are saving many souls in prayer." He invites them to pray for their loved ones, the deceased, the sick, and for all people.

sections.subtitle: Čist pogled i prava sloboda: gledati ženu kao sestru i majku
sections.screenshot_description: Gost poziva da se druga osoba gleda kao sestra i majka
sections.content:
Ono što Gospodin kroz tijelo želi naglasiti, kaže don Vitomir, jest **čistoća**. To znači imati čist pogled prema drugom spolu, bez duha požude, i voljeti drugu osobu zato što je Gospodin u njoj, a ne zbog tjelesne želje. Podsjeća da čovjek griješi već kada nešto zamisli u pogledu ili mislima, zato treba gledati Gospodina u drugoj osobi kako nikada ne bi s njom zgriješio.

Tumači i **slobodu**: ona nije činiti što čovjek hoće, nego ono što Bog želi. Bog je dao slobodu i savjest koja govori što je dobro. Za razlikovanje dobra i zla potreban je **dar mudrosti**, kakav je imao **Salomon**. Njegova mudrost, ističe, nije imala premca jer ga je nadahnuo Bog, kao što je nadahnuo pisce Staroga i Novoga zavjeta i svece. Kao primjer navodi **svetu Faustinu**, koja je podnosila osude susestara, klevete i laži, ali je ostala Božja do kraja.

Na toj podlozi ponovno se vraća pornografiji. Lažna je sloboda uključiti mobitel, gledati pornografiju, samozadovoljavati se i požudno željeti. To, upozorava, **razara mozak, odnos prema vlastitoj ženi i prema drugim ženama**, pa čovjek uvijek gleda kroz grijeh i zapravo nije slobodan. Drukčiji pogled dobiva tko drugu osobu gleda **kao sestru i kao majku**. Zato preporučuje molitvu: „Bože, daj mi te oči da mogu razabirati.“
sections.subtitle_en: A Pure Gaze and True Freedom: Looking at a Woman as a Sister and Mother
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest calls for looking at another person as a sister and mother
sections.content_en:
What the Lord wants to emphasize through the body, Don Vitomir says, is **purity**. That means having a pure gaze toward the opposite sex, without the spirit of lust, and loving another person because the Lord is in them, not because of bodily desire. He recalls that man sins already when he imagines something in a look or thoughts, which is why one should look at the Lord in another person so as never to sin with them.

He also interprets **freedom**: it is not doing what man wants, but what God desires. God gave freedom and a conscience that tells what is good. To distinguish between good and evil, the **gift of wisdom** is needed, such as **Solomon** had. His wisdom, he emphasizes, had no equal because God inspired him, just as He inspired the writers of the Old and New Testaments and the saints. As an example, he mentions **Saint Faustina**, who endured the condemnations of her fellow sisters, slanders, and lies, but remained God's to the end.

On that foundation, he returns again to pornography. It is false freedom to turn on a mobile phone, watch pornography, masturbate, and lustfully desire. That, he warns, **destroys the brain, the relationship with one's own wife and with other women**, so man always looks through sin and is not actually free. A different look is gained by whoever looks at another person **as a sister and as a mother**. Therefore he recommends the prayer: "God, give me those eyes so that I can discern."

sections.subtitle: Bolest kao prilika, a tijelo kao sveti prostor
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir objašnjava Pavlov poziv Korinćanima na čistoću i bijeg od nemorala
sections.content:
Kad Bog dopusti bolest, don Vitomir smatra da on s time ima namjeru: **čovjekovo obraćenje**, vlastitu proslavu i povratak drugih vjeri. Podsjeća da su se i za Isusovih čudesa mnogi obraćali i krenuli za njim.

Prema kršćanskom nauku, objašnjava, Duh Sveti prebiva u vjernicima nakon što prihvate Krista i čini njihovo tijelo **svetim prostorom, poput starozavjetnog hrama**. Tijelo pripada Bogu, pa ga treba poštovati i čuvati. U kontekstu poslanice Pavao time poziva na čistoću i suzdržavanje od bludnosti, nemorala i svega što čovjeka uništava duševno i tjelesno.

Zato je potrebno brinuti o zdravlju, dostojanstvu i daru tijela. Don Vitomir citira Pavlov poziv vjernicima u Korintu da **bježe od seksualnog nemorala**: tijelo je hram Duha Svetoga, „niste svoji, jer kupljeni ste otkupninom. Proslavite, dakle, Boga u tijelu svome.“ To znači slaviti Boga rukama, čistim pogledom, pjesmom i jezikom, kako bi Bog uvijek prebivao u čovjeku.
sections.subtitle_en: Illness as an Opportunity, and the Body as a Sacred Space
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir explains Paul's call to the Corinthians to purity and fleeing immorality
sections.content_en:
When God permits illness, Don Vitomir considers that He has an intention with it: **man's conversion**, His own glorification, and the return of others to faith. He recalls that during Jesus' miracles, too, many converted and followed Him.

According to Christian teaching, he explains, the Holy Spirit dwells in believers after they accept Christ and makes their body **a sacred space, like the Old Testament temple**. The body belongs to God, so it should be respected and preserved. In the context of the epistle, Paul thereby calls for purity and refraining from fornication, immorality, and everything that destroys man spiritually and physically.

Therefore it is necessary to care for health, dignity, and the gift of the body. Don Vitomir quotes Paul's call to the believers in Corinth to **flee sexual immorality**: the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, "you are not your own, for you were bought with a price. Glorify God, therefore, in your body." That means praising God with hands, with a pure gaze, with song and tongue, so that God may always dwell in man.

sections.subtitle: Tetovaže u tvrdnjama egzorcista i kultura vanjskog izgleda
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira tvrdnje egzorcista oca Gabriela Amortha o tetovažama
sections.content:
Don Vitomir se ponovno vraća temi tetovaža, ovaj put pozivajući se na izvore koje navodi. Prenosi da je **otac Gabriel Amorth**, kojeg naziva velikim egzorcistom, izjavio kako u egzorcizmima đavao kroz usta opsjednutih opetovano tvrdi da je svatko tko se tetovira njegova posvećena osoba i da je njegov utjecaj na život tetovirane osobe stvaran i kontinuiran.

Navodi i osobu koju u transkriptu imenuje kao **Anthony Levey**, „osnivača sotonske crkve u Americi“. Prema don Vitomirovim riječima, on je u knjizi *Moderni primitivi* priznao da iza svake tetovaže, bio to cvijet ili zmija, stoji sotonizam te da sotonin svećenik ima obvezu posvetiti se tetovažom. Don Vitomir dodaje navod istog egzorcista da se tetoviranjem anđela, lica svetaca te slika Isusa i Marije **Bog vrijeđa dvaput**. Naglašava da te tvrdnje prenosi od egzorcista.

Sve to vidi kao znak da je **odnos prema vlastitom tijelu narušen**. Ljudi neprestano slušaju poruke „budi lijep, budi zgodan, oblači se ovako“ i stvaraju izazove, a tijelo „nakazuju“ debljinom, frizurom i estetikom. Pavlova riječ o hramu, ističe, ne odnosi se samo na tijelo odvojeno od duše, nego na **cjelovitog čovjeka: duh, dušu i tijelo**.
sections.subtitle_en: Tattoos in the Assertions of Exorcists and the Culture of External Appearance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes the assertions of exorcist Father Gabriel Amorth about tattoos
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir returns again to the theme of tattoos, this time citing the sources he mentions. He conveys that **Father Gabriel Amorth**, whom he calls a great exorcist, stated that in exorcisms the devil through the mouths of the possessed repeatedly asserts that everyone who gets tattooed is his consecrated person and that his influence on the life of the tattooed person is real and continuous.

He also cites a person whom he names in the transcript as **Anthony Levey**, "the founder of the satanic church in America." According to Don Vitomir's words, in the book *Modern Primitives* he admitted that behind every tattoo, be it a flower or a snake, stands satanism and that Satan's priest has an obligation to consecrate himself with a tattoo. Don Vitomir adds the citation of the same exorcist that by tattooing angels, faces of saints, and images of Jesus and Mary, **God is offended twice**. He emphasizes that he conveys these assertions from exorcists.

He sees all this as a sign that the **relationship toward one's own body is impaired**. People constantly listen to messages "be beautiful, be attractive, dress like this" and create challenges, while "disfiguring" the body with obesity, hairstyle, and aesthetics. Paul's word about the temple, he emphasizes, does not refer only to the body separated from the soul, but to the **whole person: spirit, soul, and body**.

sections.subtitle: Najčešći grijesi protiv čistoće i sebeljublje kao njihov korijen
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir nabraja savjete iz knjige Nasljeduj Mariju za borbu protiv napasti
sections.content:
Pri kraju nagovora don Vitomir pornografiju jasno naziva **ovisnošću** i, pozivajući se na jednog svećenika, nabraja najčešće grijehe bludnosti:

- pornografija,
- predbračni odnosi,
- preljub u braku,
- grijeh u srcu („Tko poželi ženu u srcu, već je zgriješio“),
- odijevanje kojim se želi izazvati požuda,
- grijesi abortusa i kontracepcije.

Kritizira i one koji sve to čine, a zatim se pričešćuju bez pokajanja.

Kao duhovni putokaz navodi knjigu ***Nasljeduj Mariju***. Prema njoj je glavni uzrok tih grijeha **sebeljublje**, koje vodi u propast ako mu se popušta jer navodi čovjeka da ugađa tijelu. Za kontrolu tijela potrebne su dobra volja i milost Božja. Gospa, kako se navodi, poručuje: „Ne pusti se strastima, nego ih koristi za dobro.“

Za trenutke napasti knjiga, prema don Vitomiru, daje četiri savjeta:

1. odstraniti iz srca zle misli i paziti što se kroz oči unosi,
2. biti uzdržljiv u jelu i piću, odnosno postiti,
3. biti bogobojazan,
4. ustrajati u molitvi.

Zaključuje da se protiv tih grijeha itekako može boriti.
sections.subtitle_en: The Most Common Sins Against Purity and Self-Love as Their Root
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir enumerates advice from the book Imitation of Mary for the fight against temptation
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the talk, Don Vitomir clearly calls pornography an **addiction** and, citing a priest, enumerates the most common sins of impurity:

- pornography,
- premarital relations,
- adultery in marriage,
- sin in the heart ("Whoever looks at a woman lustfully in his heart has already committed sin"),
- dressing intended to provoke lust,
- sins of abortion and contraception.

He also criticizes those who do all this and then receive Communion without repentance.

As a spiritual guidepost, he cites the book ***Imitation of Mary***. According to it, the main cause of these sins is **self-love**, which leads to ruin if indulged, because it leads man to please the body. Good will and the grace of God are needed to control the body. Our Lady, as is stated, conveys: "Do not surrender to passions, but use them for good."

For moments of temptation, according to Don Vitomir, the book gives four pieces of advice:

1. remove evil thoughts from the heart and watch what is brought in through the eyes,
2. be temperate in food and drink, that is, fast,
3. be God-fearing,
4. persevere in prayer.

He concludes that one can certainly fight against these sins.

sections.subtitle: Brojke porno industrije i što znanost kaže o mozgu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost iznosi statistike porno industrije u SAD-u i rezultate znanstvenih istraživanja
sections.content:
Don Vitomir iznosi podatke koje navodi kao statistiku porno industrije u **Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama** za posljednjih deset godina:

- 118 osoba umrlo je od side,
- 25 osoba bile su žrtve ubojstva,
- 34 osobe su se predozirale,
- 37 godina je prosječna životna dob porno glumice,
- 41 osoba poginula je u nesretnom slučaju,
- 59 osoba počinilo je samoubojstvo.

Navodi i da je od 2011. do 2018. objavljeno oko **40 znanstvenih radova i više od 30 neuroloških istraživanja** o utjecaju pornografije. Prema zaključcima koje prenosi, pornografija utječe na fizičko i psihičko zdravlje, stvara ovisnost i strah, narušava međuljudske odnose, intimu, veze i brak te je povezana s ranim stupanjem u spolne odnose, sklonošću verbalnoj i seksualnoj agresiji i objektivizacijom žene.

Objašnjava i mehanizam: pri gledanju pornografije aktivira se **sustav nagrađivanja u mozgu**, odnosno dijelovi odgovorni za ugodu. Taj sustav inače potiče čovjeka da traži hranu, ljubav, prijateljstvo i druge stvari koje su mu po prirodi potrebne.

Pravi razlog zašto je pornografija loša don Vitomir ipak traži dublje. Poziva se na **svetog Ivana Pavla**, kojemu pripisuje misao „Osoba je čin, ljubav je odgovornost“, te na **Katekizam Katoličke Crkve**: „Pornografija se sastoji u izvlačenju spolnih čina, stvarnih i glumljenih, iz intimnosti partnera da se naumice pokaže trećim osobama.“ Bog je ljude stvorio na svoju sliku da ljube jedni druge, a pornografija ih razdvaja i vodi u to da „samo ja uživam i ne marim za drugu osobu“.
sections.subtitle_en: Porn Industry Figures and What Science Says About the Brain
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest presents statistics of the porn industry in the USA and the results of scientific research
sections.content_en:
Don Vitomir presents data that he cites as statistics of the porn industry in the **United States of America** over the last ten years:

- 118 people died of AIDS,
- 25 people were victims of homicide,
- 34 people overdosed,
- 37 years is the average lifespan of a porn actress,
- 41 people died in an accident,
- 59 people committed suicide.

He also states that from 2011 to 2018 about **40 scientific papers and more than 30 neurological studies** on the impact of pornography were published. According to the conclusions he conveys, pornography affects physical and psychological health, creates addiction and fear, damages interpersonal relationships, intimacy, relationships, and marriage, and is associated with early entry into sexual intercourse, a tendency toward verbal and sexual aggression, and the objectification of women.

He also explains the mechanism: when watching pornography, the **reward system in the brain** is activated, namely the parts responsible for pleasure. That system normally encourages man to seek food, love, friendship, and other things that are naturally necessary to him.

The real reason why pornography is bad, Don Vitomir nevertheless seeks deeper. He cites **Saint John Paul**, to whom he attributes the thought "The person is an act, love is responsibility," and the **Catechism of the Catholic Church**: "Pornography consists in removing real or simulated sexual acts from the intimacy of the partners, in order to display them deliberately to third parties." God created human beings in His image to love one another, whereas pornography separates them and leads to "only I enjoy myself and do not care about the other person."

sections.subtitle: Moć riječi „ne“ i konkretni koraci u borbi sa zlom
sections.screenshot_description: Don Vitomir nabraja konkretne korake zaštite od pornografije i završava zazivom Duha Svetoga
sections.content:
Protiv ovisnosti se treba boriti, ali, naglašava don Vitomir, **ne sam**. Prenosi riječi jednog predavača da čovjekovo „da“ ništa ne znači ako osoba ne može reći „ne“. Tko pristaje, postaje ovisnik, a tko kaže „ne, to neću“, ostaje slobodan. Odluku treba donijeti sam čovjek, ali zlo pobjeđuje s Gospodinom. Pornografija, ponavlja, ubija ljubav, razara odnose i brakove i postala je prava ovisnost.

Nudi i **konkretne korake**:

- zaštititi se **filterima** na mobitelu i internetu,
- suzbijati misli na pornografiju i usmjeriti ih na nešto vrednije,
- prema preporuci Crkve: **post o kruhu i vodi**, **molitva krunice**, **sakrament svete ispovijedi** i **sakrament svete pričesti**, odnosno primanje Isusa.

Nagovor završava jednostavnim pozivom: neka svi zazovu **Duha Svetoga** da ih vodi. Amen.
sections.subtitle_en: The Power of the Word "No" and Concrete Steps in the Fight Against Evil
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Vitomir enumerates concrete steps of protection against pornography and ends with an invocation of the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
Addiction must be fought against, but, Don Vitomir emphasizes, **not alone**. He conveys the words of a lecturer that a person's "yes" means nothing if the person cannot say "no." Whoever consents becomes an addict, while whoever says "no, I will not do that," remains free. The decision must be made by the person himself, but evil is overcome with the Lord. Pornography, he repeats, kills love, destroys relationships and marriages, and has become a true addiction.

He also offers **concrete steps**:

- protect oneself with **filters** on mobile phones and the internet,
- suppress thoughts of pornography and direct them to something more worthy,
- according to the recommendation of the Church: **fasting on bread and water**, **prayer of the Rosary**, the **sacrament of Holy Confession**, and the **sacrament of Holy Communion**, namely receiving Jesus.

The talk ends with a simple call: let everyone call upon the **Holy Spirit** to guide them. Amen.
